  "content": "115:47DEQ|
116:FxvMW|## Tools the model sees
117:47DEQ|
118:YkCsG|By default, the model gets all tools: the coding tools of pi-action (`read`, `write`, `edit`, `bash`), then the tools of each pi-durable extension. Two inputs change this:
119:47DEQ|
120:M2_Pw|| Input | Effect |
121:TUbPP||-------|--------|
122:gJmXT|| `exclude_tools` | pi-action disables these tools completely. Neither the model nor other tools can call them |
123:-g-BB|| `model_tools_hidden` | pi-action does not offer these tools to the model. Other tools can still call them, for example pit's `tools.*` |
124:47DEQ|
125:10wDN|For example, to give the model only pit's `typescript` tool, and keep the coding tools available to its programs:
126:47DEQ|
127:j44LH|```yaml
128:JOTfh|- uses: cv/pi-action@v2
129:PI-Nw|  with:
130:TlaBm|    github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
131:vQQQ3|    extensions: |
132:-yTuR|      github:cv/pit#v0.35.1
133:1VKqY|    model_tools_hidden: read, write, edit, bash
134:8bkBh|```
135:47DEQ|
136:xmdVV|- Write one name per line, or separate names with commas. `*` matches any characters, as in pit's `allowedTools`. For example, `mcp_*`.
137:iNlrb|- pi-action resolves the names against the tools after it installs the extensions, and after the [overrides](#override-tools-and-sections). For a name that matches no tool, pi-action writes a warning.
138:rWi2Q|- If the inputs leave the model with no tools, the run fails.
139:wNsBd|- pi-action applies the inputs on each run. When an input is empty, pi-action clears the setting of an earlier run on the thread.
140:GLm7E|- The `🤖` line of the log shows the tools that the model gets, for example `🤖 anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 · tools: typescript · extensions: pit (typescript)`.
141:47DEQ|
142:wwOCX|An extension can also hide a tool itself, with a wrap that sets `callers: ["tools"]` (see [Override tools and sections](#override-tools-and-sections)). The inputs apply after the wraps, and they only remove tools. Thus, an input cannot give the model a tool that a wrap hid.
143:47DEQ|
144:-YQn4|## Questions on GitHub",

130:TlaBm|    github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

136:xmdVV|- Write one name per line, or separate names with commas. `*` matches any characters, as in pit's `allowedTools`. For example, `mcp_*`.
